defects.title: Redaction blur written to the file is much weaker than the preview shows
defects.claim: The saved PNG gets a single box-blur pass per axis (`blur_rows(&patch, &mut across, pw, ph, radius); … blur_rows(&turned, &mut done, ph, pw, radius);` in shot.rs), while the preview is a CSS Gaussian of the same variance (`backdropFilter: blur(${sigmaOf(step.radius) * box.scale}px)` with `Math.sqrt((radius*(radius+1))/3)` in ShotAnnotate.tsx). Matching variance does not match legibility: a box kernel has sinc side-lobes, a Gaussian none. For r = 4/8/16 (the 1080p minimum and default) the box lets through about 22% of contrast at periods of 6.3/11.9/23 px versus about 3.5% for the equal-variance Gaussian (roughly 6x less) - exactly text-stroke and letter scale. So the UI hint "What you see here is what lands in the file" (ShotViewer.tsx:1107) is false in the dangerous direction. Additionally the Rust doc comment (shot.rs:129-134) saying the preview "blurs the whole picture and clips afterwards" is likely inaccurate: Chromium's backdrop-filter samples only within the element (mirror edges), so near edges the two differ the other way.
defects.scenario: A user blurs a 14 px password or e-mail at the default radius. The preview looks fully smeared, but the saved PNG keeps ghosted strokes that are readable, or brute-forceable against the known game/UI font.
defects.fix: Approximate a Gaussian with 3 box passes per axis keeping the variance: `r_i = ((1.0 + 4.0*r*(r+1)/3.0).sqrt() - 1.0) / 2.0`, rounded and >= 1; run `blur_rows` 3x each way and widen the margin to `3*r_i` (still O(n)). Consider a minimum radius tied to the rectangle height (e.g. >= h/4) or pixelate-then-blur, and offer a solid "redact" fill. Fix the doc comment.

defects.title: Sidecars committed before the main PNG; several screenshot writes are not atomic
defects.claim: In edit_screenshot the write order is `shot.write_png(&base_path)` (`File::create` truncates base.png in place), then `write_edit(...)` (shot.json), then `write_picture` (temp + `replace_file`, retried 10x then fails with "Is it open somewhere right now?"). The comment at commands.rs:555 ("Everything that can fail happens before the first byte is written") is not true for these three writes. `keep_original` copies to `image.png` with a plain `std::fs::copy`, and `write_under` writes `under.png`/`under.json` non-atomically as well.
defects.scenario: (a) The screenshot is open in an external viewer that locks it, or AV holds it: `replace_file` fails, but base.png and shot.json already describe the new crop and marks while the PNG is the old one; the UI catches the error and keeps its old `edit`, so the next open shows a state the file doesn't have. (b) Disk full while writing base.png leaves a truncated base.png, so draw mode shows "File not found". (c) A crash or disk-full during `keep_original`'s `std::fs::copy` leaves a partial image.png; `has_original` is then true forever and every later edit, including Reset, fails in `read_png(original)`.
defects.fix: Write all three to temp names first (`base.png.part`, `shot.json.part`, `<name>.<uuid>.new.png`). Then `replace_file` the main PNG (most likely to fail); only on success rename the sidecar parts (or remove base.png); on failure delete the parts. `keep_original`: copy to `image.png.part` and rename. `write_under`: same for under.png and under.json.

defects.title: Save racing a file move or delete orphans the edited PNG and leaves the DB pointing at the unedited file
defects.claim: `edit_screenshot` reads `clip.path` once at the start (commands.rs:518) and writes to it about 0.5-2 s later; nothing locks the clip. Closing the viewer runs `for (const id of seen) if (left.has(id)) void fileClip(id);` (Clips.tsx), and `file_clip` moves the file (favorites or game folder) and updates the DB path. The viewer's close button, Escape after Discard, and the footer Delete button all stay enabled while `busy`.
defects.scenario: The user changes the game or hits the heart in the viewer, clicks Save marks, and closes right away. `filing::place` renames P1 to P2 (and may prune P1's folder); `write_picture` then creates a new file at P1 (rename onto a missing target succeeds) and runs `set_picture` with the edited dimensions. Result: the DB points at the unedited P2 with wrong dimensions, the thumbnail comes from the orphan at P1, and P1 stays in the user's folder forever. Delete during a save similarly recreates `originals/<id>/…` and the PNG as orphans.
defects.fix: Add a per-clip busy set in `AppState`: `write_screenshot` holds it; `file_clip` and `delete_clip` wait for it or skip. Re-read `lib.get(id).path` immediately before `replace_file`, inside the library lock. Disable Close and Delete while `busy`, or defer `fileClip` until the save resolves.

defects.title: Editor usable before its edit store loads; failed load swallowed; save then drops crop/marks and misplaces blurs
defects.claim: The load is `api.screenshotEdit(id).then(...).catch(() => {})` and tools are enabled with `disabled={!inTauri || broken}` with no check of `edit`. While `edit` is null: `full = clip.width` (the cropped size), `origin = {0,0}`, draw mode draws on `clip.path` (marks already baked in), and Save sends `write(edit?.crop ?? null, shapes)`, i.e. crop = null. If the load resolves late, `resetShapes(readMarks(loaded))` silently wipes whatever was drawn in the meantime.
defects.scenario: `screenshot_edit` errors (e.g. "clip database is not available") or resolves late because the main thread is busy. On a cropped shot with only blur marks, saving silently removes the crop, drops previously saved marks from shot.json, and applies the crop-relative blur rectangles to the uncropped original at the wrong spot, so the redaction misses its target. With non-blur marks Rust fails with "The layer does not fit the picture."
defects.fix: Disable tools and Save until `edit !== null`; show the load error instead of swallowing it; have `write` refuse to run while `edit` is null.

defects.title: Save's async continuation is not tied to the clip it started for; old edit lands on the next picture
defects.claim: After `await writeScreenshot(...)` the code runs `const loaded = await api.screenshotEdit(clip.id); setEdit(loaded); resetShapes(readMarks(loaded));` using the closure's (old) `clip`, with no check that the viewer still shows it. Discard is always enabled (1089) and the step/navigation buttons are enabled once `mode === "view"` (1249, 1259).
defects.scenario: Save, then Discard (mode -> view), then navigate to the next shot. The new shot's load resolves fast; the old continuation resolves later and wins, so the viewer holds the previous screenshot's `edit` (its `basePath`, crop and marks) for the new picture. Entering draw mode shows the wrong base; saving writes the foreign crop and marks into the new screenshot.
defects.fix: Keep `const shownId = useRef(id)` and bail out after each await when `shownId.current !== clip.id`. Better: have `write_screenshot` return the new `ShotEdit` directly.

defects.title: Marks drawn while a save is running are silently discarded
defects.claim: AnnotateLayer stays interactive while `busy` (ShotViewer.tsx:880-892). When the save finishes, `resetShapes(readMarks(loaded)); … setMode("view")` (632-638) replaces everything drawn since Save was clicked.
defects.scenario: On a 4K picture (about a 1 s save) the user adds one more arrow right after clicking Save; the arrow vanishes without a prompt and there is no undo.
defects.fix: Block input while `busy` (`pointer-events: none` overlay or BusyVeil), or snapshot `current.current` at save time and re-apply any newer shapes as unsaved.

defects.title: PNG decompression bomb in read_png/read_rgba (allocation before any size check), reachable via friend-shared screenshots
defects.claim: `read_png` allocates the frame buffer from IHDR alone: `let mut buffer = vec![0u8; reader.output_buffer_size()];` (shot.rs:455-472); png 0.17's `Limits` only cap row and chunk buffers, not this caller-allocated buffer. `read_rgba` (shot.rs:676-689) checks the layer's dimensions against the picture only after the full allocation and decode (`blend`, shot.rs:105-108). Received shared files go straight into the library (share.rs:633-692).
defects.scenario: A malicious or compromised friend sends a ~100-byte "screenshot" whose IHDR claims 60000x60000 (about 14 GB RGBA). The user right-clicks it and chooses Copy picture (`copy_clip_image`) or edits it; `vec!` fails and `handle_alloc_error` aborts the whole app, replay buffer included. If the allocation succeeds instead, the RGB conversion and `dib()` allocate another 2-3x.
defects.fix: After `read_info`, reject anything with `w as u64 * h as u64 > 1<<28` (and dimensions > 16384), then allocate with `try_reserve_exact`. Give `read_rgba` the expected `(w, h)` and reject on mismatch before allocating. At receive time read the header and store the real dimensions.

defects.title: Layer PNGs travel over IPC as JSON number arrays and are buffered by serde as Content
defects.claim: `layerBytes` returns `Array.from(new Uint8Array(await blob.arrayBuffer()))`, so each byte becomes about 3.6 JSON characters plus a JS Number, stringified on the UI thread. On the Rust side `Step` is internally tagged (`#[serde(tag = "kind")] … Layer { png: Vec<u8> }`), so serde first buffers the whole object into `Content` (one ~32-byte `Content::U64` per PNG byte) and then copies into `Vec<u8>`.
defects.scenario: A 2 MB layer (text-heavy, large fills, 8K) costs roughly 7 MB of JSON plus 64 MB of transient Rust memory per save.
defects.fix: Send layers as raw IPC bodies (`invoke("write_shot_layer", bytes, { headers: { id, index } })`, Rust reads `tauri::ipc::Request` -> `InvokeBody::Raw`), or at minimum base64 strings with `#[serde(with = "...")]` and an adjacently/externally tagged enum. Encode in a worker with `OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob`.

defects.title: Preview and save use full-resolution canvases per blur-separated run
defects.claim: Preview canvases are `<canvas width={width} height={height}>` at full picture pixels (ShotAnnotate.tsx:566-586). Every blur splits the layer runs, so N blurs mean N+1 canvases of 3840x2160 (33 MB each; 132 MB each at 8K) plus the draft canvas. Save allocates another N full-size canvases at once (`Promise.all(... layerBytes ...)`, ShotViewer.tsx:609-618); at 8K this can fail, and `getContext`/`toBlob` returning null throws and is swallowed (see the swallowed-failures finding).
defects.scenario: On 4K/8K screenshots with several blurs, the WebView holds hundreds of MB of canvas memory; saving at 8K can fail silently.
defects.fix: Size preview canvases to `round(box.width*devicePixelRatio)` with `ctx.setTransform(scale…)`, repainting on zoom. Serialise `layerBytes` (or use OffscreenCanvas in a worker).

defects.title: Drag repaints the whole run on a full-res canvas and re-renders the entire ShotViewer tree on every pointer move
defects.claim: A move or resize drag repaints the entire run containing the mark (all of its siblings) on a full-resolution canvas. Each move also calls `editShapes` -> `setShapes` in ShotViewer, re-rendering the whole ~1650-line tree (sidebar, ColorPicker, ClipMeta).
defects.scenario: Dragging or resizing a mark on a large screenshot causes a full-res repaint and a full React re-render per pointermove, making interaction sluggish.
defects.fix: During a drag, lift the dragged mark into its own layer (as is already done for drafts) and throttle with rAF; memoise the side panel.

defects.title: Failed thumbnail rebuild silently keeps the pre-edit (unredacted) thumbnail
defects.claim: After an edit, thumbnail failure is only logged: `if let Err(err) = make_still(..) { log::warn!(..) }` (commands.rs:640-643), and `set_picture` (clips.rs:290-302) doesn't touch `thumb_path`. The old `thumbs/<id>.jpg` stays; gallery and console tiles use `?v=${clip.sizeBytes}`, which changes, so they re-fetch the old JPEG. Also, if the capture-time thumbnail failed, `thumb_path` stays NULL forever even after a successful rebuild.
defects.scenario: ffmpeg is unavailable or fails at edit time (it was fine at capture): a 480-px thumbnail of the unblurred content remains visible in the gallery and console.
defects.fix: Build the thumbnail in-process from the `picture` already in memory (box downscale + the existing `png` crate; drop the ffmpeg dependency for stills). On any failure delete the old thumbnail and set `thumb_path` to NULL. Have `set_picture` also set `thumb_path`.

defects.title: Editor trusts database dimensions when there is no original; received screenshots carry sender-claimed dimensions
defects.claim: `screenshot_edit` falls back to `} else { (clip.width, clip.height) }` when there is no original (commands.rs:457-461). Received screenshots store sender-supplied meta as dimensions (`width: meta.width, height: meta.height`, share.rs:129-136, 841-851) without reading the file header.
defects.scenario: A friend's screenshot with wrong meta: the canvas, `full` and the CropLayer are sized wrongly, and `object-contain` letterboxes the real image inside a box of the wrong aspect. Marks and blurs misalign, and Rust rejects layers ("does not fit").
defects.fix: In `screenshot_edit` always use `size_of_png(clip.path)` when there is no original. At receive time verify the header (PNG magic, sane dimensions) and store the real dimensions.

defects.title: Received screenshots may be JPEG, which permanently breaks editing and Copy picture
defects.claim: The receive path accepts `jpg/jpeg` for screenshots (share.rs:1187-1190), but the editor and clipboard assume PNG.
defects.scenario: For a received `.jpg` screenshot, `keep_original` copies the JPEG to `image.png`, after which `read_png` fails forever; Copy picture also fails.
defects.fix: At receive time verify the header (PNG magic, sane dimensions) and reject non-PNG screenshots.

defects.title: AnnotateLayer and CropLayer never clear an interrupted drag
defects.claim: AnnotateLayer only handles pointer down/move/up (ShotAnnotate.tsx:917-925), and `onMove` never checks `event.buttons` (764-767); CropLayer (ShotViewer.tsx:1408-1414) has the same gap. The stage's own pan handler already handles the case ("Let go somewhere the stage never heard of it (Alt+Tab mid-drag)", ShotViewer.tsx:786-790), but the two layers don't.
defects.scenario: After Alt+Tab or a lost pointer capture mid-drag, `drag.current` or `draft` stays set; the selected mark (or the crop) follows the hovering mouse with no button held and keeps adding to the same undo step until the next click.
defects.fix: Add `onPointerCancel` and `onLostPointerCapture` handlers that reset `drag.current` and the draft, and ignore moves with `event.buttons === 0`.

defects.title: Unredacted original kept forever in originals/<id>/image.png with no way to purge it
defects.claim: The pre-edit original is stored at `%APPDATA%\ClippiBoy\originals\<id>\image.png` (shot.rs:287-289) indefinitely. `discard_original` (edit.rs:139-151) only knows `video.mp4` and returns "There is no original to throw away." for screenshots, so the only way to purge the unredacted pixels is to delete the screenshot.
defects.scenario: A user blurs or crops sensitive content believing it is gone; the unredacted full image remains on disk in the app data folder with no UI to remove it.
defects.fix: Add a "Flatten - discard history" action that removes `image.png`, `base.png` and `shot.json` (keeping `under.*`). Mention in the UI that blur and crop stay reversible locally.

defects.title: External edits to the screenshot are silently overwritten on the next ClippiBoy save
defects.claim: `edit_screenshot` rebuilds from the stored original (`image.png`) every time (commands.rs:539) without checking whether the main file was changed externally; the DB dimensions also go stale.
defects.scenario: After the first ClippiBoy edit, the user edits the PNG in Paint or Photos. The next ClippiBoy save rebuilds from the stale image.png and drops those external changes.
defects.fix: Record size and mtime (or a hash) of the last written file in shot.json; on mismatch warn, or adopt the external file as the new original.

defects.title: Blocking sync commands marked #[tauri::command(async)] run on tokio workers
defects.claim: `write_screenshot`, `copy_clip_image` and `take_screenshot` are sync fns with `#[tauri::command(async)]`, which (likely, per Tauri 2.11 macro behaviour) runs them on async runtime workers. They do blocking work there: PNG decode/encode, blur loops, `replace_file`'s sleep-retry (up to about 2.75 s), the blocking ffmpeg wait, and `Clipboard::open`'s sleeps.
defects.scenario: A slow save or clipboard retry stalls other async tasks sharing the runtime (share, links, updater).
defects.fix: Make them `async fn` and wrap the body in `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking`.

defects.title: Save-path failures other than writeScreenshot are swallowed in ShotViewer
defects.claim: The save catch is `catch { /* "The notice is already in the store." */ }`, which is true only for `writeScreenshot`. A throw in `layerBytes` (`getContext`/`toBlob` returning null) or in the follow-up `screenshotEdit` shows nothing.
defects.scenario: Layer encoding fails (e.g. at 8K) or the reload after save fails: no error is shown and the UI stays "unsaved" although the file may have been written.
defects.fix: Set `lastError` in that catch for non-writeScreenshot failures.

defects.title: Copy picture menu action has an unhandled rejection and no success/failure feedback
defects.claim: `onSelect: () => void api.copyClipImage(clip.id)` leaves the promise rejection unhandled and shows no toast on success or failure.
defects.scenario: Copy fails with e.g. "Another program is holding the clipboard" and the user gets no message; on success there is no confirmation either.
defects.fix: Add `.then(() => notify("Picture copied"), err => set({ lastError }))`.

defects.title: Undo merges drags across an AnnotateLayer remount because gesture ids restart at 0
defects.claim: Gesture ids come from `gestures.current`, which restarts at 0 whenever AnnotateLayer remounts (draw -> crop -> Cancel -> draw), while `lastGesture` in ShotViewer survives the remount. The first drag afterwards (`drag-1`) therefore merges with the last drag before the remount (`drag-1`).
defects.scenario: User drags a mark, switches to crop, cancels, returns to draw and drags again; one Undo reverts both drags.
defects.fix: Use a module-level or `useId`-based gesture counter and reset `lastGesture` on mode change.

defects.title: Restyle undo key merges separate style changes into one undo step
defects.claim: `restyle` uses the history key `style-${id}-${keys}`, which is identical for separate clicks on the same mark and property.
defects.scenario: Changing one mark red -> blue -> green with three separate clicks produces a single undo step.
defects.fix: Give restyle a per-interaction token (pointerdown or slider-start).

defects.title: Temp-file names collide across concurrent saves and leftovers are never cleaned up
defects.claim: The main PNG temp is `target.with_extension(format!("{}.new.png", std::process::id()))` (commands.rs:633) and shot.json uses a fixed `shot.json.part` (shot.rs:353). Two concurrent saves of the same clip in one process write the same temp files, and nothing ever cleans up leftovers.
defects.scenario: A crash between write and rename leaves `Name.1234.new.png` in the user's Screenshots folder permanently; concurrent saves of one clip clobber each other's temp files.
defects.fix: Use uuid or atomic-counter suffixes plus a startup sweep of `*.new.png` and `*.part`. A per-clip lock (from ED-3) also fixes the collision.

defects.title: Hooks called after an early return in ShotViewer
defects.claim: `if (!clip) return null;` at ShotViewer.tsx:421 is followed by `useEffect` (453) and `useRef` (462). If `clip` ever went from defined to undefined React would throw "Rendered fewer hooks than expected". It can't happen today (Clips.tsx always passes `min(open, len-1)` with `len > 0`), so the early return is effectively dead, and rules-of-hooks lint fails.
defects.scenario: A future change that lets `clip` become undefined after mount crashes the viewer with a hooks-order error; lint currently fails.
defects.fix: Move those hooks above the guard.

defects.title: Hit-test margin uses blur size (a radius) as stroke width, creating a huge invisible halo
defects.claim: `const margin = shape.tool === "text" ? slack : Math.max(slack, shape.size);` treats a blur's `size` as stroke width, but for blur it is a radius running up to `base*12` (96 px at 4K, 192 px at 8K).
defects.scenario: A recent blur's invisible halo steals Select clicks meant for nearby marks.
defects.fix: Use `slack` for blur (and text).

defects.title: Watermark scale() degenerates when upscaling, producing a blocky mark unlike the smooth preview
defects.claim: `scale()` in watermark.rs:179-205 assumes downscaling. For frames taller than about 2171 px (152/0.07, e.g. 5K, 8K or tall crops) it degenerates to nearest/box sampling, so the burned-in mark is blocky while the `` preview is smooth.
defects.scenario: Saving a 5K/8K screenshot or a tall crop produces a visibly blocky watermark that differs from the preview.
defects.fix: Use bilinear sampling when `step < 1`.

defects.title: Blur edge handling differs between preview and file
defects.claim: The preview's backdrop-filter clips and mirrors at the patch edge, while the Rust blur reads `radius` pixels beyond the patch. A saved blur cut by a crop reads black stage in the preview but real pixels in Rust.
defects.scenario: Near patch or crop edges the saved blur looks different from the preview the user approved.
defects.fix: No specific fix given beyond aligning preview and file behaviour (see ED-1).

defects.title: Caption text jumps vertically on commit (CSS line-height vs canvas textBaseline top)
defects.claim: The caption edit field uses `lineHeight: 1.25` (CSS half-leading) while the canvas draws with `textBaseline = "top"` (em-box top), so the two place text at different vertical offsets.
defects.scenario: Text moves a few pixels vertically when the caption is committed from the field to the canvas.
defects.fix: No specific fix given (align the field's line box with the canvas baseline).

defects.title: Clipboard read_text scan is not bounded by the global block size
defects.claim: `read_text` scans up to 4,000,000 `u16` after `GlobalLock` without consulting `GlobalSize`, looking for a NUL terminator.
defects.scenario: Another app places a non-NUL-terminated `CF_UNICODETEXT` on the clipboard; ClippiBoy reads up to 8 MB past the block, which can be an access violation.
defects.fix: `let max = GlobalSize(block) / 2;` and loop only to `max`.

defects.title: OpenClipboard called with a NULL owner window (unsupported for SetClipboardData)
defects.claim: The clipboard is opened with `OpenClipboard(HWND::default())`. MSDN says that with a NULL owner, `EmptyClipboard` sets the owner to NULL and `SetClipboardData` "fails". It works in practice, but it's unsupported.
defects.scenario: On some Windows configurations SetClipboardData could fail after EmptyClipboard with a NULL owner, breaking Copy picture/text.
defects.fix: Pass the main window's HWND to OpenClipboard.

defects.title: Thumbnail ffmpeg filter fails or upscales for extreme crops
defects.claim: The thumbnail filter is `-vf scale=480:-1`, fixing width at 480 regardless of aspect or source size.
defects.scenario: A 16x4000 crop asks for 480x120000, which exceeds the JPEG limit, so ffmpeg fails and the stale-thumbnail problem (ED-11) applies; tiny crops get upscaled.
defects.fix: Use `scale='min(480,iw)':'min(480,ih)':force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease`.

defects.title: Out-of-range rectangles are clamped to a 1-pixel strip instead of rejected
defects.claim: Clamping uses `x.min(self.width.saturating_sub(1))`, so a rectangle entirely right of or below the picture becomes a 1-px strip at the edge: `clamped` and `crop` succeed and `blur` writes one column, instead of returning an error. The UI never sends such a rect, but a buggy or compromised caller could.
defects.scenario: A malformed write_screenshot call with a rect outside the picture silently crops to / blurs a 1-px edge strip rather than failing.
defects.fix: `if area.x >= self.width || area.y >= self.height { return Err(..) }`.

defects.title: Dead IPC call screenshotHasOriginal invokes an unregistered command
defects.claim: `screenshotHasOriginal` in ipc.ts:150-151 invokes `"screenshot_has_original"`, which isn't registered in `lib.rs`.
defects.scenario: Any caller of screenshotHasOriginal would get a command-not-found rejection; the code is dead.
defects.fix: Remove the dead call (or register the command).

defects.title: crop's doc comment merged into clamped's doc; crop has none
defects.claim: `crop`'s doc ("Cut a rectangle out of the picture…") is merged into `clamped`'s doc comment at shot.rs:34-47, and `crop` itself has no doc comment.
defects.scenario: Misleading API docs for clamped/crop.
defects.fix: Split the doc comment so each function documents itself.

defects.title: clamped and crop duplicate the same clamping logic
defects.claim: `clamped` and `crop` in shot.rs repeat the same clamping logic.
defects.scenario: The two copies can drift apart.
defects.fix: `crop(Rect)` should take the already-clamped rect.

defects.title: MAX_ZOOM_STEP duplicates MAX_ZOOM
defects.claim: `MAX_ZOOM_STEP = 8` (ShotViewer.tsx:60) duplicates `MAX_ZOOM = 8` (pictureBox.ts:78).
defects.scenario: Changing one constant without the other makes zoom limits inconsistent.
defects.fix: Use a single shared constant.

defects.title: Watermark asset size 535x152 hard-coded in TS
defects.claim: The watermark asset size 535x152 is hard-coded in watermark.ts:142-143.
defects.scenario: A regenerated watermark asset with different dimensions would silently break the preview's mark placement.
defects.fix: Derive the size from the asset (or share the constant with Rust).

defects.title: Marks stored as JSON-in-JSON with full float precision
defects.claim: shot.json stores the marks as a JSON string inside JSON (`Edit.marks: String`), and point coordinates are saved at full float precision (bloat).
defects.scenario: shot.json is larger and harder to read/migrate than necessary.
defects.fix: Use `serde_json::value::RawValue` for marks; round point coordinates.

defects.title: No frontend tests
defects.claim: There are no frontend test files or test runner, so editor logic such as `markRect`, `fitRatio`/`spanned`, `toSteps`, `shift`/`readMarks`, `sigmaOf` and the move-clamp in `onMove` is untested.
defects.scenario: Regressions in preview/file parity (e.g. markRect vs Rust rect_kept) or coordinate maths go unnoticed.
defects.fix: Add vitest coverage for `markRect` vs fixtures from the Rust `rect_kept` tests, `fitRatio`/`spanned`, `toSteps`, `shift`/`readMarks` round-trip, `sigmaOf`, and the move-clamp in `onMove`.

defects.title: ShotViewer.tsx is a 1650-line component holding too much state
defects.claim: ShotViewer.tsx (about 1650 lines) holds the viewer, the load/save state machine, undo history, crop layer, side panel, Disclosure/PanelButton and `layerBytes`. Several bugs (ED-4, ED-5, ED-6) stem from that state being spread across closures.
defects.scenario: Race and state bugs are hard to see and fix; the whole tree re-renders on edits.
defects.fix: Extract `useShotEdit(id)` (load, save, race guards, busy, error), `useUndoHistory`, `CropLayer.tsx`, `AnnotatePanel.tsx`, and a `layers.ts` (render and encode).

defects.title: Avoidable work on every save (base.png re-encode, ffmpeg spawn, Reset re-encode)
defects.claim: On every save `base.png` is re-encoded even on marks-only saves where the crop is unchanged; an ffmpeg process is spawned per save for the thumbnail; and the Reset path re-encodes the original instead of copying it.
defects.scenario: Each marks-only save on a large screenshot pays a full PNG encode of base.png plus an ffmpeg process launch; Reset is slower than a file copy.
defects.fix: Skip writing base.png if `read_edit(id).crop == crop && base exists`; build thumbnails in-process (see ED-11); copy the original on Reset.

defects.title: Each editor mode decodes a different full-resolution PNG in the WebView
defects.claim: View, draw and crop modes each use a different ground image (finished file, base.png, image.png), so every mode switch decodes a different full-res PNG in the WebView.
defects.scenario: Switching modes on large screenshots causes repeated full-resolution decodes and delays.
defects.fix: No specific fix given.

defects.title: Pen strokes copy the whole points array per sample and miss coalesced events
defects.claim: Pen strokes copy the whole points array on every sample (O(n^2)) and don't use `getCoalescedEvents()`, so fast strokes come out angular. `bounds()` uses `Math.min(...xs)` spreads, which can hit V8's argument limit on extremely long strokes (speculative).
defects.scenario: Long pen strokes get progressively slower; fast strokes look jagged; an extremely long stroke could throw from `bounds()`.
defects.fix: Append points without copying, use `getCoalescedEvents()`, and compute bounds with a loop instead of spread.

defects.title: Size slider steps from a fractional minimum, so values snap off the default
defects.claim: The slider uses `step = 1` (Controls.tsx:95) with `range()` min `Math.max(1, base*0.4)` (ShotAnnotate.tsx:127), which can be fractional (e.g. 0.8 or 3.2), so values snap to 0.8, 1.8 …
defects.scenario: The slider knob shows a value different from the default size until it is touched.
defects.fix: Pass `step = min` or round `min`.

proposals.title: Fix priority order for the screenshot editor
proposals.value: Orders the editor fixes by risk so the redaction and data-integrity problems are addressed first.
proposals.sketch: 1. Blur kernel (ED-1). 2. Commit order and atomic writes (ED-2). 3. Per-clip lock and disabling close/delete/draw while busy (ED-3, ED-6). 4. Gate the editor on a loaded `edit` and guard the async continuation by id (ED-4, ED-5). 5. PNG size caps (ED-7). 6. Raw-binary IPC for layers (ED-8). 7. Display-resolution preview canvases (ED-9/ED-10). 8. In-process thumbnails with failure cleanup (ED-11).

positives: Clip ids are sanitised everywhere (`muxer::sanitize`: ASCII alphanumerics, everything else `_`) and every shot command looks the id up in the library first; no path traversal.
Serde shapes match the TS types: `Step` is internally tagged; ShotEdit, Rect and Clip are camelCase.
TS `markRect` matches Rust `rect_kept` exactly, including f32 vs f64 rounding (the .5 cases were checked).
Zoom and pan maths in the viewer are correct.
`blur_rows` is tested against a naive implementation.
No `u32` width x height overflow is reachable.
clipboard.rs: the `unsafe` in `put` is correct (frees the handle on lock or Set failure, size >= len), as are the `DROPFILES` layout and the DIB stride and padding.
